entries.arabic: العاشر على صورة السرطان، قسمه بارد رطب ودولته تسعة آلاف سنة، ملك متحرك بيده مفتاح خلق الدنيا.
entries.english: The tenth is in the form of the Crab [Cancer]. His division is cold and moist and his dominion nine thousand years. He is an angel in motion; in his hand is the key to the creation of the present world.
entries.grade: source-aligned first-pass; printed-image and manuscript collation pending

entries.arabic: الحادي عشر على صورة أسد، قسمه حار يابس ودولته ثمانية آلاف سنة، ملك يعلوه مهابة، بيده مفتاح خلق الآخرة.
entries.english: The eleventh is in the form of a Lion [Leo]. His division is hot and dry and his dominion eight thousand years. He is an angel upon whom awe is manifest; in his hand is the key to the creation of the next world.
entries.grade: source-aligned first-pass; printed-image and manuscript collation pending

entries.arabic: الثاني عشر على صورة سنبلة، قسمه بارد يابس ودولته سبعة آلاف سنة، وله اختصاص معين بالاجسام الانسانية.
entries.english: The twelfth is in the form of the Ear of Wheat [Virgo]. His division is cold and dry and his dominion seven thousand years; he has a particular relation to human bodies.
entries.grade: source-aligned first-pass; printed-image and manuscript collation pending

entries.arabic: فمن الأسد والقوس والحمل وجدت كرة الأثير، وبالجوزاء والميزان والدلو وجدت كرة الهواء، وبالسرطان والعقرب والحوت وجدت كرة الماء، وبالثور والسنبلة والجدى وجدت كرة الأرض، فالله هو الفاعل سبحانه لكل شئ وهذه أسباب تعينها ليبتلى بها عباده - كما مر -.
entries.english: From Leo, Sagittarius, and Aries the sphere of aether came into being; from Gemini, Libra, and Aquarius the sphere of air; from Cancer, Scorpio, and Pisces the sphere of water; and from Taurus, Virgo, and Capricorn the sphere of earth. God alone—glory be to Him—is the agent of all things: these are the causes of the determinations of those things, through which He tests His servants, as already explained.
entries.notes: Distinguish the claim that God is the sole agent from the intermediary order of cosmological determinations in the quotation.
entries.grade: source-aligned first-pass; printed-image and manuscript collation pending

entries.arabic: قال: ثم أحدث الله سبحانه الفلك الرابع وخلق عالم الرضوان بينه وبين # فلك البروج وسطحه ارض الجنة ومقعره سقف النار وفيه أسكن رضوان خازن الجنان، وملائكة هذا الفلك تسمى التاليات، وهذا الترتيب لا يمكن ادراكه الا بالكشف أو بخبر الصادق، والله تعالى لما خلق هذا الفلك رتب في مقعره الف مرتبة واحدى وعشرين مرتبة، قسم الفلك عليها اقساما - كما قسم فلك البروج على اثنى عشر قسما - فظهر لكل قسم كرة فظهرت اثنتا عشرة كرة هي فلك الثوابت والسبعة الأفلاك التي تحته والأربعة الأركان، فكذلك قسم هذا الفلك الرابع الأقسام التي ذكرناها وجعل في كل قسم ملكا على صورة عالم من عوالم الأركان، فدار هذا الفلك دورة أبرز فيها عالم الجنان كحركة الأرض في اخراج النباتات، كما قال تعالى: اهتزت وربت وأنبتت من كل زوج بهيج (5 - الحج) وهذا الفلك هو فلك الحروف، ومن هنا انتشأت على الثمانية والعشرين منزلة ثمانية وعشرون حرفا.
entries.english: He says: God—glory be to Him—then brought forth the fourth sphere and created the world of Riḍwān between it and the sphere of the zodiacal signs. Its upper surface is the earth of Paradise and its concave interior is the roof of the Fire. There He established Riḍwān, keeper of the gardens. The angels of this sphere are called the Reciters [al-tāliyāt]. This arrangement cannot be apprehended except by unveiling or the report of one who speaks truth. When God created this sphere He arranged in its concavity one thousand and twenty-one degrees, dividing the sphere into corresponding parts as He had divided the zodiacal sphere into twelve. For each part a sphere appeared; thus twelve spheres came into view: the sphere of the fixed stars, the seven celestial spheres beneath it, and the four elements. In like manner He divided the fourth sphere into the divisions already mentioned, setting within each division an angel corresponding in form to one of the elemental worlds. This sphere made a revolution through which the world of gardens became manifest, as the earth by its movement brings forth plants. As He—exalted is He—said: “It stirred, swelled, and brought forth every delightful kind” (Qurʾān 22:5). This is the sphere of letters; from here twenty-eight letters arose in correspondence with the twenty-eight lunar mansions.
entries.notes: The reading “one thousand and twenty-one” corresponds to ألف مرتبة واحدى وعشرين مرتبة in the electronic text; verify the number in print. Qurʾān 22:5 is cited as a cosmological analogy, not as a scriptural statement of this celestial schema.
entries.grade: source-aligned first-pass; printed-image and manuscript collation pending

entries.arabic: اما الحروف الخارجة عن حد الاستقامة في الانسان وغيره من الحيوانات فهي بعدد ما بقى من الأقسام، مقدرا بمقدار لا يزيد ولا ينقص، وذلك في الانسان كالحروف بين الباء والفاء وبين الجيم والشين، وكحروف الخيشوم - وكذا في الحيوانات -
entries.english: The letters that fall outside the bounds of straightforward articulation, in human beings and in other animals, correspond in number to the remaining divisions, by a measure that neither increases nor decreases. In the human being these include sounds between bāʾ and fāʾ, between jīm and shīn, and sounds produced in the nasal cavity; likewise among animals.
entries.notes: “Outside straightforward articulation” renders خارجة عن حد الاستقامة; it may refer to uncanonical or intermediate phonetic values, pending comparison with the source context.
entries.grade: source-aligned first-pass; printed-image and manuscript collation pending

entries.arabic: وأخبرني بعض العلماء عن تلميذ جعفر الصادق عليه السلام: انه اوصلها إلى بضع وسبعين حرفا، والحروف لا تعطى خواصها الا ما يعطيه حكم المنازل، غير أن لها روحانية لطيفة في الفلك الأطلس الذي هو سقف الجنة بها يبقى الكلام على أهل الجنة - أعني الحروف الفعلية -
entries.english: One of the learned informed me, on the authority of a disciple of Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq—peace be upon him—that he brought their number to more than seventy letters. Letters exhibit their special properties only according to what is imparted by the ruling of the [lunar] mansions. Yet they possess a subtle spiritual reality in the starless sphere, which is the roof of Paradise, through which speech endures for the inhabitants of Paradise—that is, the letters as acts.
entries.notes: The report concerning Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq is transmitted within the quoted passage, not independently verified.
entries.grade: source-aligned first-pass; printed-image and manuscript collation pending

entries.arabic: واما اللفظية فهي لهم من نفس هذا الفلك الذي هم فيه، ولكن أعذب والطف من هذا الكلام المعتاد، لأنها تفعل هناك بالروحانية الخالصة - كشكلنا في الجنان على اعدل نشأة - فانتج الاستعداد الحسن والفيض الروحاني نتيجة تناسبها، ومن هذا الفلك # كان في الجنة الأنهار والرياح والشجر والحور والقصور والولدان والأكل والشرب والنكاح والانتقالات من حال إلى حال على أهل الطبيعة، الا ان الامر ثابت في عين الحوامل والقوابل - لحفظ الاعتدال - فلا يستحيلون ابدا ولكن يختلف عليهم الصور والحالات والاشكال والمطاعم والملابس والمناكح والاعراض.
entries.english: As for articulated letters, they arise for [the inhabitants of Paradise] from the very breath of the sphere in which they dwell, but their speech is sweeter and subtler than ordinary speech, because there it operates through pure spirituality—as does our bodily configuration in the gardens, in the most perfectly balanced constitution. A wholesome preparedness and spiritual effusion thus produce a result proportionate to both. From this sphere come the rivers, winds, trees, houris, palaces, youths, eating, drinking, marriage, and transitions from one state to another which the inhabitants of the natural order experience in Paradise. Nevertheless, the substrata of reception and the receptive subjects themselves remain stable, preserving equilibrium. They never undergo corruption or transmutation in their being, though forms, states, shapes, foods, garments, partners, and accidents vary for them.
entries.notes: The final distinction is between persistence of the receptacle and alteration of states and forms; do not read this as a contemporary physical theory.
entries.grade: source-aligned first-pass; printed-image and manuscript collation pending

entries.arabic: هذا ما نقلناه عن لفظ الشيخ الكبير رضي الله عنه في صفة الأفلاك الأربعة الدائمة.
entries.english: This is what we have transmitted from the Great Master's own wording concerning the four enduring spheres.
entries.notes: Explicit close of the preceding Ibn ʿArabī quotation.
entries.grade: source-aligned first-pass; printed-image and manuscript collation pending

entries.arabic: فان قلت: عبارات شيخنا قدس سره في مفتاح الغيب والتفسير والفكوك وشرح الحديث وغيرها يشعر بان الفلك الثابت الدائم هو العرش والكرسي ليس الا وان الجنة بينهما موافقا لما جاء في الحديث: سقف الجنة عرش الرحمن وان مقعر الكرسي وما تحته طبقات جهنم، وان جرم الكرسي هو الأعراف، فكيف التوفيق بينه وبين ما ذكره الشيخ الكبير رضي الله عنه هنا وفي الفصوص وغيره من أن الأفلاك الأولية الثابتة الدائمة الأربعة؟
entries.english: If you say: The expressions of our Master—may his secret be sanctified—in Miftāḥ al-ghayb, the Commentary, the Fukūk, the commentary on the ḥadīth, and other works suggest that the enduring, fixed celestial spheres are only the Throne and the Footstool; that Paradise is between them, in agreement with the report that “the roof of Paradise is the Throne of the All-Merciful”; that the concavity of the Footstool and what lies beneath it constitute the levels of Hell; and that the body of the Footstool is al-Aʿrāf. How can this be reconciled with what the Great Master—may God be pleased with him—states here, in the Fuṣūṣ and elsewhere, namely that the primary, enduring, fixed spheres are four?
entries.notes: This is Fanārī's explicit objection contrasting Qūnawī's two-sphere account with Ibn ʿArabī's four. Correct book title is al-Fukūk (الفكوك), not a text called “Fukūk”; formatting normalisation below may be needed.
entries.grade: source-aligned first-pass; printed-image and manuscript collation pending

entries.arabic: قلت: كما أن ظاهر لفظ شيخنا انها فلكان لا غير، كذلك ظاهر لفظ الشيخ الكبير رضي الله عنه انها أفلاك أربعة متباينة وأجسام متناضدة، لهذا قال: لا يمكن معرفتها الا بالكشف أو خبر الصادق، ولا يطلع عليها بالرصد، وكذا ما يشعر به كلام الشارح الجندي في تعيين العرش والكرسي: انها أربعة متباينة وأجسام متناضدة، لكن الشارح الفرغاني ذكر في ديباجة شرح القصيدة: ان كلا من العرش والكرسي اعتبر صورتهما المثالية تارة بحكم المرتبة التي ظهرت الهيئة فيها فسميتا العرش والكرسي، واعتبر صورتهما الجسمانية المركبة من الطول والعرض والعمق أخرى، فسمى العرش باعتبارها فلك الأفلاك والفلك الأطلس والمحدد، وسمى الكرسي باعتبارها فلك الكواكب والمنازل.
entries.english: I answer: Just as the outward wording of our Master suggests that there are only two spheres, so the outward wording of the Great Master suggests that there are four distinct celestial spheres, composed of bodies placed one above the other. Hence he says that they cannot be known except through unveiling or a truthful report, not through astronomical observation. The wording of the commentator al-Jandī, when he identifies the Throne and the Footstool, similarly suggests four mutually distinct, superimposed bodies. But the commentator al-Farghānī states in the preface to his commentary on the Poem that each of the Throne and the Footstool is considered, in one respect, according to its imaginal form, by virtue of the degree in which that configuration appears, and in that respect both are named Throne and Footstool. In another respect their bodily forms, compounded of length, breadth, and depth, are considered: the Throne in this respect is named the sphere of spheres, the starless sphere, and the determining sphere; and the Footstool in this respect is named the sphere of the stars and mansions.
entries.notes: The exegetical solution treats “four” designations as potentially four considerations of two realities; inspect Farghānī's preface for independent verification.
entries.grade: source-aligned first-pass; printed-image and manuscript collation pending

entries.arabic: وهذا مما يوفق بين كلامي الشيخين ويبين ان شيخنا قدس سره كما هو عادته نص على حقيقة الحال ولم يفصل حسب اعتباري الشئ الواحد في الأقوال، وأشار بذلك ان كلام الشيخ الكبير رضي الله عنه راجع إلى هذا في المآل، وذلك لما حكى ان شيخنا قدس سره # بعد ما عرض عليه الفرغاني ديباجة شرحه قررها والحق بها فصلا ناطقا باستحسانه، فذلك مما يصح متمسكا في هذا التوفيق. والله أعلم بمراده ومراد أهل التحقيق.
entries.english: This provides a reconciliation of the two Masters' statements and shows that our Master—may his secret be sanctified—has, as is his custom, stated the reality of the matter without differentiating its verbal formulations according to the two considerations of a single thing. He thereby indicated that what the Great Master says ultimately comes back to this. It is reported, moreover, that after al-Farghānī presented the introduction to his commentary to our Master, the latter approved it and appended a chapter expressly stating his favourable judgement. That is something one may rightly use in support of this reconciliation. God knows best what he and the people of verification intended.
entries.notes: The approval report supplies an argument of textual reception, not proof that the doctrinal reconciliation is necessary.
entries.grade: source-aligned first-pass; printed-image and manuscript collation pending

entries.arabic: ثم لاشتمال كلام كل من الشارحين في تعينهما على علوم جمة واسرار مهمة، رأينا ان ننقلهما بنوع من الانتخاب.
entries.english: Because the discussions of both commentators concerning their identification of these realities contain extensive knowledge and significant secrets, we have thought it appropriate to reproduce them selectively.
entries.notes: Transition to selected passages of al-Jandī and al-Farghānī, commencing §4.611.
entries.grade: source-aligned first-pass; printed-image and manuscript collation pending
